templates.label: Codex 5.3 Spark
templates.summary: Spark: quick bounded edits, scans, and follow-up review with low evidence overhead.
templates.description: Use for bounded or mechanical implementation, quick scans, and follow-up review. Spark is a low-evidence lane, not a broad default, and should hand off when the task needs sustained reasoning or cross-file judgment.

templates.label: Codex 5.4 Mini
templates.summary: Mini: bounded implementation and support work with low-evidence review.
templates.description: Use when the task is bounded and speed matters more than maximum reasoning depth. Mini is a low-evidence lane for narrow code changes, focused audits, log summarization, and helper work feeding a stronger reviewer.

templates.label: Codex 5.5
templates.summary: GPT-5.5 medium: default implementation with bounded reasoning and independent review.
templates.description: Use for normal implementation lanes that need source reading, edits, tests, and follow-through. GPT-5.5 medium is the bounded implementation default, not the low-evidence claim, and it should still hand off to independent review when risk rises.

templates.label: Codex 5.5 High
templates.summary: Terra High: complex implementation, review-driven follow-through, and broad coordination.
templates.description: Use when a worker should act as a review-driven implementer, use Codex App Server thread/goal tooling, investigate opaque failures, or coordinate several Codex worker lanes. Terra High fits complex implementation and broad coordination before independent review.

templates.label: GPT-5.6 Sol High
templates.summary: Sol High: difficult implementation and cross-file debugging.
templates.description: Use for difficult implementation, opaque failures, and changes spanning several files or contracts.

templates.label: GPT-5.6 Sol XHigh
templates.summary: Sol XHigh: architecture and root-cause diagnosis before patching.
templates.description: Use for architecture diagnosis, hard root-cause analysis, and plans that need stronger reasoning before patching.

templates.label: GPT-5.6 Sol Max
templates.summary: Sol Max: concurrency, replay, process, and exact-contract review.
templates.description: Use as a deep-review lane for acceptance-critical diffs, concurrency and replay checks, process-sensitive behavior, and exact-contract review before acceptance.

templates.label: GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra
templates.summary: Sol Ultra: split work, produce candidates, and compose evidence without self-acceptance.
templates.description: Use as an orchestration lane for splitting complex work, supervising worker outputs, and reviewing final evidence. Sol Ultra may decompose work and produce candidates, but it never owns terminal self-acceptance.

templates.label: GPT-5.6 Terra Medium
templates.description: Use for default Terra implementation lanes with explicit medium reasoning effort. Terra Medium is evidence-limited and should not be treated as a broad default.

templates.label: GPT-5.6 Terra High
templates.summary: Terra High: complex implementation and review-driven integration debugging.
templates.description: Use for broader implementation and integration debugging where Terra should spend more effort before patching.

templates.label: GPT-5.6 Terra Max
templates.summary: Terra Max: lifecycle, security, migration, and regression review.
templates.description: Use for migration, compatibility, lifecycle, security, and regression review when the patch is risky but does not need orchestration.

templates.label: GPT-5.6 Luna Low
templates.summary: Luna Low: docs, bounded diagnosis, and smoke checks.
templates.description: Use for quick audits, deterministic checks, documentation work, bounded diagnosis, and smoke checks using exact GPT-5.6 Luna behavior.

templates.label: GPT-5.6 Luna Medium
templates.summary: Luna Medium: evidence-limited implementation with practical review.
templates.description: Use for small implementation tasks where Luna should balance speed and reasoning. Luna Medium is evidence-limited, not a broad default.

templates.label: GPT-5.6 Luna Max
templates.summary: Luna Max: convergence and order review before promotion.
templates.description: Use for final focused review of a bounded diff before promotion; choose Sol or Terra for ultra orchestration. Luna Max is the convergence and order review lane.

templates.label: Claude Fable 5
templates.summary: Fable: architecture, supply-chain, and exact-byte challenge review.
templates.description: Use as the deep-research lead: Fable synthesizes final findings and plans, can guide Haiku extraction and Sonnet follow-through, and should use approved source URLs only. Also use for difficult architecture, supply-chain checks, exact-byte challenges, and multi-hour reasoning; expect slower replies.

templates.label: Claude Opus 4.8
templates.summary: Opus: read-only consultation or tightly bounded external execution with exact stop conditions.
templates.description: Use for demanding implementation review, architecture alternatives, and correctness checks where quality matters more than latency. Opus is permitted only as read-only consultation or tightly isolated externally bounded execution with exact stop conditions and independent proof; do not use it for unattended container work, shared-runtime work, destructive cleanup, background builds, or repeated-heavy authority.

templates.label: Claude Sonnet 5
templates.summary: Sonnet: provider-diverse fallback for balanced coding, planning, and follow-through.
templates.description: Use for implementation follow-through after Fable or Opus research, medium-depth code review, and practical planning. Sonnet is the balanced Claude fallback when a role needs provider diversity or when Codex quota blocks the planned lane.

templates.label: Claude Haiku 4.5
templates.summary: Haiku: cheap extraction, triage, and scout work without owning required evidence gates.
templates.description: Use for parallel source extraction, finding exact quoted evidence, summarizing logs, and quick sanity checks. Haiku is best as a scout feeding a Fable, Opus, Sonnet, or Codex supervisor rather than owning hard synthesis or a required evidence gate after an audited no-output run.
